# Panel (`packages/panel`)

Solid UI rendered in the DevTools panel. The browser glue (`browser.devtools.*`) lives in `apps/extension/entrypoints/panel/`; `packages/panel` has no `chrome.*`/`browser.*` code.

## Connection list (`src/ConnectionList.tsx`, `src/Panel.tsx`)

- `Panel(props: { renderers: RendererView[]; tree: TreeStore; inspector: InspectorStore })` renders `ConnectionList` in the themed full-height `<main>`. `apps/extension/entrypoints/panel/main.tsx` connects a `runtime` port named `panel`, subscribes with `browser.devtools.inspectedWindow.tabId`, sets a signal from each `TabStateMessage`, and applies each tree batch to the store (`docs/messages.md`, "Tree flow").
- States: no renderers and `stale` (the tab was open before ReactDX was installed or updated; `docs/messages.md`, "Reconnects"): an `Empty` screen (`src/Empty.tsx`, shared with the inspector: centered, icon in a `bg-surface` circle, title, muted hint, `EmptyAction` button): a reload arrow, "Reload this page to inspect React.", "It was open before ReactDX was installed or updated." and "Reload page" (`onReload`, `inspectedWindow.reload()` in `main.tsx`; `onNavigated` clears `stale`). No renderers otherwise (#95): an `Empty` screen (`ReactGlyph`, `src/Toolbar.tsx`) "No React on this page.", "ReactDX finds React as the page loads. If this page uses React, reload it." and "Reload page" (`onReload`, shared with the stale screen). Only production (#95): an `Empty` screen (`ReactGlyph`) "Production build of React <versions>." and "ReactDX inspects development builds. Open the app from its dev server to inspect it.", no action. Otherwise one `[data-testid=renderer]` per copy (`React <version> <development|production> <rendererPackageName>`) with `[data-testid=root]` rows ("Root N", "N commits", `data-commits`). Production copies are listed with their roots (Next's dev overlay) but get no agent.
- Under each development root, a `TreeView` of its components. Production roots list no components.
- With a development copy, a split (`[data-testid=split]`): the toolbar and copies on one side, the `Inspector` in `<aside data-testid="inspector" aria-label="Inspector">` on the other. Side by side from Tailwind's `sm` (640 px), stacked below that (DevTools docked at the side); each pane scrolls on its own. In the trees pane the toolbar stays put and `[data-testid=trees]` below it is the one scroller, both ways, for every copy's headings and trees (trees don't scroll themselves; e2e: `the trees pane is the only scroller`). Its list is `w-max min-w-full`, so wide trees widen the scroll, not the rows. No inspector for no-React and production-only pages.
- Page data is only ever a Solid text node, never markup (unit test and `e2e/forged.test.ts` check an `<img onerror>` version renders as text).
- `test/ConnectionList.test.tsx` (Vitest `panel` project): each state, component rows under development roots only, text-only, no Tailwind palette classes or arbitrary values.
- Reconnect: `main.tsx` `connect()` opens the `panel` port and subscribes; when the port drops (the background stopped), it connects again, which wakes the background and asks the relay for current state.
- Reset: `browser.devtools.network.onNavigated` clears the list and subscribes again on the current port, so a new document shows only what it reports ("No React on this page" until its React connects).

## Tree store (`createTreeStore()`, `src/tree.ts`; M3 #25)

The page's component tree, rebuilt from the agent's ops (`docs/messages.md`, "Tree batches"). Exported as `@reactdx/panel/tree`.

- `apply(batch)` applies `reset`, `add`, `remove` (with descendants), `reorder` and `rename`, and bumps a Solid `version` signal. It returns true when the panel must ask for a resync: the first time a batch has the wrong `seq` or an op names an unknown id (an `add` under an unknown parent, a `reorder` of one, a `remove` or `rename` of an unknown node). After that it ignores batches until one starting with `reset`, so a burst of bad batches asks once.
- `rows(rootId)`: `Row = { id, name, depth, kind, key, expandable, expanded, match }`, depth-first. Host (DOM element) nodes are hidden unless `showHosts()`: their children take their place and depth. `expandable` means it has a visible descendant through hidden hosts. Collapsed nodes' descendants aren't listed; everything starts expanded. `match`: the node matches the search.
- `showHosts()` / `setShowHosts(on)` (M3 #27): one visibility rule for rows, `expandable` and Left's parent. Hiding hosts clears a selected host (it has no row). Off on every panel open.
- `toggle(id)`: collapses or expands.
- `selected()` / `select(id)`: one selection for the panel (ids are unique per document). After each batch it's cleared only if its node is gone, so it survives commits and a resync that re-adds the id (ids persist across watches, `docs/page.md`).
- `key(rootId, key): boolean`: moves the selection within that root's rows; true when the key is handled. A selection in another root counts as none.
  - `ArrowUp`/`ArrowDown`: previous/next row, clamped; with none selected, the first row.
  - `Home`/`End`: first/last row.
  - `ArrowLeft`: collapses an expanded row, else selects the nearest non-host ancestor.
  - `ArrowRight`: expands a collapsed row, else selects its first child; nothing on a leaf.
- Search (M3 #27): the current match is the selection, so arrowing or clicking elsewhere and pressing Enter continues from there.
  - `query()` / `setQuery(q)`: sets the query and selects the first match.
  - `matches()`: ids of visible-kind nodes whose name contains the query, case-insensitive. Every root depth-first, roots in first-seen order, collapsed subtrees included. Empty query: none.
  - `step(1 | -1)`: next or previous match, wrapping; from a non-match, the first or last.
  - `position()`: the selection's index among the matches from 1, or 0 if it isn't one.
  - Selecting a match (`setQuery`, `step`) also expands its ancestors, so it has a row, and TreeView scrolls it into view.
- `hovered()` / `hover(id | undefined)` (M3 #28): the row under the pointer. `main.tsx` sends a highlight or clear-highlight command on each change (`docs/messages.md`, "Tree flow").
- `picking()` / `setPicking(on)`, `picked(id | null)` (M3 #29): `main.tsx` sends `pick-start`/`pick-stop` whenever `picking` changes (a redundant `pick-stop` after a pick is ignored by the agent). `picked` turns picking off and, for an id the mirror has, selects and reveals it (expands ancestors; TreeView scrolls it into view); a DOM element's id (from the Elements panel, #92) while DOM elements are hidden reveals its nearest non-host ancestor instead. `null` or an unknown id only turns picking off.
- `reveal(id)` (M4 #35): selects a node from outside the tree (the inspector's owners) and expands its ancestors; unknown ids do nothing.
- `clear()`: on `onNavigated`, with the renderer list; also drops collapse state, the selection, the hover and picking. The query and DOM toggle stay.
- `test/tree.test.ts`: rows, hidden hosts, each op, the resync rules, collapse, selection, every key, shown hosts, search, step.

## Inspector store (`createInspectorStore(send, copy)`, `src/inspection.ts`; M4 #33)

The selected node's values as the agent last sent them (`docs/messages.md`, "Inspected values"). Exported as `@reactdx/panel/inspection`; `main.tsx` passes a `send` that posts `{ ...command, tabId }` on the current port, calls `inspect(id)` on every selection change, and `resend()` when a batch starts with `reset`. Named `inspection.ts` because `inspector.ts` and `Inspector.tsx` are one file on a case-insensitive disk.

- `inspect(id | undefined)`: sends `inspect` (null for none), clears data, open paths and loaded objects. `resend()` asks again for the same id.
- `receive(inspected)`: replies for another id are ignored. `data()` is the latest; `gone()` is true for `data: null`. Every reply drops the loaded objects and asks again for each open ref, so open values show current contents.
- `open(path, ref?)`, `close(path)`, `isOpen(path)`: paths are `RowPath`s (`src/paths.ts`): `{ root, keys }`, `root` one of `"props"`, `"state"`, `{ hook: [call indexes] }`, `{ context: <read order> }`, `keys` the names or indexes (array items, map entries and set values by index, never their preview) from there. The open map is keyed by `pathKey(path)` (`JSON.stringify([root, keys])`), so a key holding a dot (`a.b`) and the nested `a` > `b` are different rows, and `"0"` isn't `0`. `childPath(path, key)` extends one. Opening a ref (a value past the page's depth limit) sends `expand { objectId: ref, offset: 0 }` once.
- `receiveExpanded(expanded)`, `expansion(objectId)`: what loaded per object; a later page (offset above 0) is appended. `more(container)` sends `expand` at its `nextOffset`, seeding the expansion with what's shown so the page appends to it.
- `edit(path, value)`, `remove(path)`, `rename(path, to)`: send `edit { id, root, path, value }`, `delete-path { id, root, path }` and `rename-path { id, root, path, to }` (`root` and `path` from the row path) for the inspected id, through one `write` (nothing when none is inspected); the page's re-send shows the result.
- Row menu actions: `copyKey(text)` copies at once (`copy`: `main.tsx`'s `editor.copy`, a selected textarea and `execCommand("copy")`). `copyValue(target)` and `storeValue(target)` send `copy-value` / `store-value` with a `ValueTarget` (`docs/messages.md`): the page has the whole value, the panel only a cut, paged copy. `receiveValueText(valueText)` copies the page's text only as the reply to a `copyValue` (once): the page can post one at any time, which would otherwise write the clipboard unasked. `receiveValueStored(valueStored)` likewise, only after a `storeValue`: `stored()` is the global's name until `clearStored()`.
- `test/inspection.test.ts`.

## Inspector (`Inspector`, `src/Inspector.tsx`, `src/values.tsx`, `src/value.ts`; M4 #33)

- Files: `Inspector.tsx` has the header, search, sections and menus; `values.tsx` (M6 #60) the rows they render (`ValueRow`, `HookRows`, `Children`, `ValueInput`, `Toggle`, `Triangle`) and their helpers (`entriesOf`, `tone`, `loadedOf`, the search filters `entryShows`/`hookShows`/`descendantShows`, `ROW`). Apart so the render-insight section and the commit timeline render values with the same rows.

- Empty states (`Empty`, `src/Empty.tsx`): centered in the pane, the picker's crosshair (`PickGlyph`, shared with the toolbar, drawn by `Glyph`) in a `bg-surface` circle, a title and a muted hint. None selected: "Select a component to inspect it.", "Click it in the tree, or pick it on the page.", and a "Pick an element" `EmptyAction` (`aria-pressed`, toggles `tree.setPicking`; while picking it reads "Click an element on the page", in accent). `gone()`: "This component unmounted.", "Select another in the tree." The title comes first: `selectListed` (e2e) spots a lost selection by its "Select a component" start.
- Answer (M6 #73, `src/answer.ts`): above the sections (after the source row; hidden while searching), `[data-testid=answer]` says in one sentence why the shown render (`inspector.render()`, the latest or the pinned commit's) happened: `answerOf(render, context)` returns `Part`s (text, `{ code }`, `{ node, name }`: a `NodeLink` when the tree knows the id, else code) for "No renders since DevTools opened.", "Mounted 2s ago.", "Remounted 2s ago: key changed (a → b)." / "...: Layout remounted.", "Forced to render 2s ago.", "Rendered 2s ago because its parent ProductList rendered. None of its props changed." (the parent is `data.owners[0]`), or "Rendered 2s ago because props count changed (1 → 2) and State #1 changed (3 → 4)." (one change with its previews; several by name, past three "a, b and 2 more"; hooks labeled as in Renders; contexts by name, no values). The time is `ago(now() - render.time)` (`src/ago.ts`, shared with Commits; `now` from `ConnectionList`'s 1 s clock), left out without `time`. Absent or released renders read as in Renders. Under it, at most one `[data-testid=hint]` (`hintOf`, first match): a render only because the parent rendered, with `tree.countOf(id).wasted` ≥ 1: "3 of its 4 renders were like this. Wrap X in memo() to skip them."; a `same-value` prop: "style is a new object with the same value each render. Move it out of the parent's render or wrap it in useMemo."; a `new-function` prop on a `memo` component: "onAdd is a new function each render. Wrap it in useCallback." A "See renders" button opens Renders.
- Renders (M6 #61; named "Why did this render" until #73): after Hooks, folded by default, from `data.render` (`docs/messages.md`, Render reasons). A `[data-testid=reason]` row per kind, in the page's order: "Mounted", "Props changed", "State changed", "Context changed", "Parent rendered", "Forced" (`KIND_TEXT`). Under props, state and context, a `ChangeRow` (`src/values.tsx`, `[data-testid=change]`) per change reads `name: old → new` (previews as in value rows): a prop or class state key by its name, a hook as the Hooks section labels it plus ` #N`, its depth-first row number there (groups included, so two `State`s read apart), a context by its name. A prop change that's only a new reference (`reference`, M6 #62) gets a muted badge (`Badge`, shared with value rows): "same value, new reference" (an equal object or array) or "new function", their titles saying `memo` sees a change (`REFERENCE_BADGE`). Either side holding an object opens to `Before` and `After` value rows (not editable). Their paths have the root `{ render: "props" | "state" | "hooks" | "contexts" }` (`PathRoot`, `src/paths.ts`), never written. A `mount` with `render.remount` (M6 #64) reads `Remounted: key changed (a → b)` (a missing key as `none`) or `Remounted: ancestor <name> remounted`, the name a button like the owners' (hover highlights, a click reveals and selects it), or `Remounted: an ancestor remounted` when the tree doesn't know the id (`Remounted`, read reactively: the row stays while the record changes). With `render.effects` (M6 #63), an "Effects ran" reason row follows, then a `[data-testid=effect]` row per effect named like a changed hook: `Effect #3: deps [1] changed` (the changed deps' indexes) or `Effect #5: no deps`, and a `ChangeRow` per changed dep named `[1]` (root `{ render: "effects" }`, keys the effect's name and the dep). With `render.updaters` (M6 #65), a last `[data-testid=trigger]` row reads `Triggered by Counter (State #1: 3 → 4) +2 more` (#69): the first updater the tree knows, its name a button (`NodeLink`, shared with `Remounted` and Commits), its hook changes as the page labeled them (type name, not Hook names) with previews; the rest as a `+N more` button (`onCommit(render.seq)`: opens that commit in Commits, where every trigger is listed). None known (a root render): `Triggered by: unknown`. `ReasonRow` wraps its children in one `<span>`: the row is `ROW` (flex), which drops whitespace-only text between items, so "Triggered by" and the name ran together. With `data.history` (M6 #66), a `[data-testid=history]` row "N renders recorded" is a button (`onRenders`: Commits, filtered to the node). The reasons shown are `inspector.render()` (Inspector store: `history()`, `pinned()`, `receiveReasoned`): the newest render follows re-sends. While an update is picked in Updates (`inspector.pinned()`), the first row (`[data-testid=pinned]`) reads "An earlier update" (#74: no seq) with a "Show latest" button (`onLatest`: `timeline.live()`), and the section shows the node's render in that commit (sent for with `reason { id, seq }`; nothing while it loads; "This render is no longer recorded." once released), or "Didn't render in this update." (`inspector.absent()`). Labels of an older render's hooks come from the current Hooks section. No `render`: "No renders recorded since DevTools opened." (recording starts with the panel). Hidden while searching: reasons aren't keys or values.
- Header (`[data-testid=inspector-header]`, fixed above the sections): the name, the tree's badge for `memo`/`forwardRef`/`lazy`, and `key="…"`, from `tree.info(id)`; then (M6 #73) `[data-testid=owners]` "in … › Layout › ProductList": the nearest two owners (`data.owners`, nearest first), outer first, links as in the answer, `… ›` when there are more.
- Show fallback and Show error (M5 #56): `IconButton`s (`SuspenseGlyph`, `ErrorGlyph` from `src/Toolbar.tsx`) before Force re-render, one for each boundary the inspection names (`boundaries.fallback`, `boundaries.error`: the nearest Suspense and error boundary at or above the node), `aria-pressed` while the page has it forced. A press sends `inspector.force(kind, !on)`; turning one on also selects the boundary (`tree.reveal(id)`): showing the fallback hides the node and showing the error UI unmounts it, and the boundary's own inspection keeps the pressed toggle to turn it off.
- Show in Elements panel (#92): an `IconButton` before Force re-render, for any node (host rows too): `onShowElement(inspector.id())` (`Panel` > `ConnectionList` > `Inspector`). Without `data.dom` it is disabled, its reason "No DOM element to show" (a Server Component, a component rendering nothing). A button, not on each selection: `inspect()` switches DevTools to the Elements panel.
- Force re-render (M5 #55): an `IconButton` (`ReloadGlyph`, shared with the reload screen from `src/Toolbar.tsx`) before Hook names, for any kind but `host`; it calls `inspector.rerender()` (`rerender { id }`), and the page renders the node again with nothing changed (one commit).
- Hook names (M4 #37): the header's "Hook names" toggle (`IconButton`, `aria-pressed`), off by default. The `settings` prop (`{ hookNames(), setHookNames(on) }`, type `Settings` in `Inspector.tsx`) comes from `createSettings(store)` (`src/settings.ts`; `main.tsx` passes `storage.local`, key `hookNames`): off until the stored value arrives, which is ignored if the developer already changed the setting (a late read on a slow machine undid the press). On, each hook row with a `site` asks `sources.hookName(site)` (one `createResource` per row, nothing asked while off) and reads `<type>(<name>)` (`State(count): 0`, `useCart(cart): "2 items"`, `Context(Theme)(theme)`); no name leaves the type.
- Naming (`src/names.ts`, `createHookNamer(fetch)`): fetches the served module at the call site (`http(s)` only), parses it once per URL for the panel's lifetime (a failure is retried), with `src/hook-names.ts` loaded by dynamic `import()`: `acorn` and the parser are their own chunk (`chunks/hook-names-*.js`), never loaded while the setting is off. Dev output keeps local names, so the served code (Vite module, Next chunk) is parsed, not the original: no TypeScript/JSX parser, no source map. `parseModule` tries `sourceType: "module"`, then `"script"`. `hookNameAt(ast, code, line, column)`: the innermost `CallExpression` containing the frame's position; only one that initializes a `VariableDeclarator` is named: an `Identifier` gives its name, an `ArrayPattern` its first element's, an `ObjectPattern` its first property's value; anything else (bare call, assignment, argument) gives null.
- Inspector rows (values, hook groups, owners) are at least `min-h-5` (20 px), the tree's `ROW_HEIGHT`.
- Order (`byName`, `sortedEntries` in `src/value.ts`): object keys (Props, State, nested objects, an array's extra props, and inline previews like `{a: 1, b: 2}`) and the Context list read alphabetically, case ignored, numbers in order (`a2` before `a10`). Hooks keep call order, arrays index order, maps and sets insertion order (their order is part of the value), and Rendered by nearest owner first. Sorting is the panel's: the page sends its own order.
- Search (#45; `src/search.ts`): a `SearchField` ("Search keys and values", `[data-testid=inspector-search]`; the toolbar's search box, shared from `src/Toolbar.tsx`) in a fixed `h-8` row under the header. The field fills its bar's height less padding (toolbar `h-10`: 28px; here 24px). Escape or "Clear value search" empties it. The query lives on `Inspector` outside its `Switch`, so it's kept across selections (and through "Select a component").
  - Matching: `matches(text, query)`, case-insensitive substring, on a row's name or `previewText`. A row also shows if a loaded descendant matches (`entryShows` → `descendantShows`): an inline container, what was loaded for it, or an opened ref's `inspector.expansion(id)`; `seen` guards circular refs. Never asks the page: an unopened ref matches on its preview only.
  - Hooks (`hookShows`): label (with its found name: found Hook names live in a map on `Inspector`, `labelOf(hook)`, shared by the rows and the section check), value preview, sub-hooks, the value's loaded descendants. Rendered by: owner name.
  - While the query is set, a row whose descendant matches, a custom hook with a matching sub-hook, and every section show open (`shownOpen`, `Section`'s `forced`) without touching `inspector.open` or the collapsed set, so clearing restores the user's view. Hook and context rows are hidden in place (`Show`), not filtered out of their lists: their paths are by index. Sections without a showing row hide; none at all: "No matches".
  - Highlighting: `searchRanges(root, query)` builds DOM `Range`s over matches in `[data-search-text]` elements (row names and values, value-less hooks, owners); `paintMatches` sets them as `CSS.highlights` `reactdx-search` (the CSS Custom Highlight API, Chrome and Firefox 140+), repainting from a `MutationObserver` on the sections' scroller and on query changes. `::highlight(reactdx-search)` in `index.css` paints `fg` on the `highlight` token. No `<mark>`: a value stays one text node, which both e2e readers (they join text nodes with spaces) and screen readers need. jsdom has no `CSS.highlights`: painting is skipped there.
- Sections (`[data-testid=section]`): Props, State, Hooks (M4 #34), Renders (M6), Context, Rendered by (M4 #35). The header button (`aria-expanded`, the tree's triangle) collapses one; collapsed sections stay collapsed while the panel is open. A section with nothing in it isn't shown (Renders always shows, outside a search). Renders, Context and Rendered by start folded (`FOLDED`, M6 #73; the `folded` prop overrides it, which the unit tests use to start open); Props, State and Hooks start open, since a function component's state lives in Hooks. The header button is named by its section (`aria-label`) and described by the summary (`aria-describedby`) while closed. A closed header shows a muted one-line `summary`: Props and State their first key and preview, Hooks the distinct hook names, Renders "5 since DevTools opened · 4 wasted" (`tree.countOf`; "none since DevTools opened"), Context the names, Rendered by the nearest owner.
- Value rows (`[data-testid=value]`): `name:` (`text-syntax-key`), a space, then `previewText(value)` as one text node, the two inside one inline `truncate` span (as flex items the space between them was dropped) (so both browsers' e2e readers get it whole), colored by kind (string, number, muted for undefined/function/symbol/getter/hole/unreadable, accent for null and booleans). Containers and refs get a toggle (`[data-testid=value-toggle]`) that opens them in place, indented 12 px per level; map entries read `key => value`; a paged container ends with "Show more (N left)". Circular refs don't open.
- Hooks: each hook in call order, `name: value`, or just its name when it has no value (an effect without deps). A custom hook (`useCart: "2 items"`, its DebugValue as the value) opens to the hooks it called; its path's root is `{ hook: [call indexes] }`. "Couldn't read hooks: <reason>" when the shadow render threw.
- Context: one value row per context read, `Theme: "dark"`; editable (M5 #54: the page writes the nearest provider's `value`) unless it's `default` (no provider above), which shows a muted `default` badge (`[data-testid=badge]`, `ValueRow`'s `badge`, titled "No provider above: its default value, read-only") and no editor; path root `{ context: <read order> }` (its index before the alphabetical sort).
- Keyboard (`keyboardRows(root)`, `src/rows.ts`, on the sections' scroller, `role="tree"` "Values"): each section header (`Section`'s button: `aria-level` 1, `data-path` `section:<name>`, its own toggle) and every value, hook and context row under it (`aria-level` depth + 2) is `role="treeitem"`, rows with `aria-expanded` when it opens, and `data-path` (`pathKey`). The rows are one tab stop: the last focused row by path holds `tabIndex` 0, else the first; a `MutationObserver` re-syncs as rows render (a row can't tell it's the first). Up/Down, Home/End move; Right opens a closed row (its toggle) or moves into an open one, Left closes an open row or moves to the nearest earlier row a level up. A re-render that replaces the focused row (a re-send) gives focus to the row with the same path, while the inspector held focus; only a replaced row (the last focused element no longer connected): a row's editor closing on blur leaves focus where it is going, since Firefox runs that blur before focus reaches the next row and restoring the edited row then won (#68); `focusin` holds it, a `focusout` to elsewhere or a `pointerdown` outside lets go. Headers are rows so Tab never strands focus on one: from a header's button Tab used to leave the inspector, its rows reachable only from another section's. Focused rows show an accent outline (`focus-visible`; no `focus:outline-none` beside it: Tailwind 4's sets `--tw-outline-style: none`, which the outline then reads).
- Editing (M5 #50, #51, #52): `ValueRow`'s `editable` comes down through `Children`'s `editable`: the Props and State sections' roots, and a `State`/`Reducer` hook row, start it; each container passes it on only when it's plain (`isPlain`, `src/typed.ts`: an array, or an object whose `className` is `Object` or null), so Map, Set and typed-array entries and class instances' fields are replace-only (the page refuses a path through them too); Context rows and other hooks aren't editable (React DevTools edits only `State` and `Reducer` hooks too: a ref's change never re-renders). A context hook (`HookValue.context`) is edited in its Context row: its value gets the editable cue, and a click or Enter on it (`ValueRow` `editAt`, from `HookRows`' `editContext`) opens the Context section if collapsed, focuses that row and sends Enter there, opening its editor. One place to edit, which shows the edit changes the provider's value for every reader. None for a default context. An editable value carries `editable-value` (`src/index.css`): the text cursor, and an input-like box (surface background, inset border, padding pulled into the space before it so nothing shifts) while its row (`group`) is hovered or keyboard-focused. A dotted underline was too subtle. Every editable value but a boolean is typed: a click on the value (`data-value`, through the row's `onClick`), Enter or F2 on the focused row swaps it for `ValueInput` (`[data-testid=value-input]`, `autocomplete="off"`, focused on mount, `aria-label` "Edit <key>") holding `editText(value)`: strings JSON-quoted (`"Count"`, so `"5"` stays a string and `5` is a number), numbers, booleans and `null` as JSON, `undefined`/`NaN`/`Infinity`/`-Infinity`/`-0` by name, a plain container the panel holds whole (no page left, no ref, extra or marker inside) as JSON; anything held only in part (a cut string, a paged or ref-holding object, a Map, Date, function or class instance) opens empty: it's replaced, never written back half loaded. Enter applies `parseTyped(text)` (JSON plus those five words; objects tagged `{ type: "object", props }`, markers as `EditValue`s; a number JSON overflows, `1e999`, reads as nothing); text that reads as nothing goes as a string over a string (a word needs no quotes) and otherwise shows "Not a valid value" (`role="alert"`) and keeps the input. Escape cancels (and stops propagation: DevTools opens its drawer on Escape) and returns focus to the row; blur cancels. An editable boolean has a checkbox (`tabIndex -1`, one tab stop stays the row) before its key; it and Space on the row send the flipped value, and the checkbox is set back to the shown value: the page's re-send is the only source of truth, no optimistic value. Edits go through `inspector.edit(path, value: EditValue)` (Inspector store).
- Row menu (`src/RowMenu.tsx`): right-clicking a value, hook or context row opens a `role="menu"` at the pointer (portaled to the body, kept inside the window, first item focused; Arrow keys move, Escape, a press outside, a scroll, a resize or blur close it): "Copy key" (the row's name: prop, index, map key preview, hook label), and for a row with a value "Copy value" and "Store as global variable" (the store's `copyValue` / `storeValue`). Targets: a container's child `{ objectId: container.id, key }` (`Entry.key`: the prop name, or the index into items, map entries or set values), a hook `{ hook: [call indexes] }` (`HookRows`' `at`), a context `{ context: <read order> }` (its index before the alphabetical sort). A hook without a value (an effect) offers Copy key only. After a store, a `role="status"` note fixed at the panel's bottom right reads "Stored as `$reactdx1`. Use it in the Console." for 4 s (`STORED_MS`); the status element is always there so screen readers announce it. An editable row (M5 #53) also offers "Add key" on a plain object (an `edit` of `""` at `newKey`, or the first free `newKey<n>`) or "Add item" on an array (`undefined` at its length), and, under a plain container, "Delete" (`inspector.remove`) and, under a plain object, "Rename key": the key turns into `ValueInput` (`[data-testid=key-input]`, "Rename <key>"), refusing an empty name or a sibling's (`siblings`, from `Children`) with "Not a valid name", else `inspector.rename(path, to)`. The new row comes with the page's re-send. Shift+F10 or the context-menu key opens it for the focused row (Keyboard), at the row's bottom left; closing it gives focus back to what had it (`RowMenu` keeps `document.activeElement` from mount and refocuses it on cleanup if still connected), unless the chosen item moved focus on (the rename input would be blurred shut).
- Source row (`[data-testid=source]`, M4 #36): the first line of the sections' scroller, so it scrolls away with them (the fixed header was name, source and search: 100px, now 64px). Not at the bottom like React DevTools: opening a picked component's file stays one glance away. `label(location)` (`Counter.jsx:13`, file name and line), its title the full `locationText` (`file:line:column`); an "Open in editor" button. When opening copied instead, "Copied", and for an absolute path a "VS Code" link (`vscode://file<path>:<line>:<column>`). Hidden while there's no source or it resolves to nothing. Resolutions are keyed by the source's value (`JSON.stringify`): an equal re-send keeps the row (no flash), and another source shows nothing until its own resolves, never the previous component's location (an "Open in editor" click would open the wrong file; M4 #38).
- Suspense (M7 #80): the store keeps each boundary's wait from the `suspense` op, `{ waiting, ms, at }` (`at`: when it came, `Date.now()`); `waitOf(id)` gives `{ waiting: true, ms: ms + now - at }` or `{ waiting: false, ms }`. While any boundary waits a 100 ms interval (`TICK_MS`) sets a `clock` signal that `waitOf` reads, stopped once none waits or on `reset`. A suspense row ends with `[data-testid=wait]`: "waiting 1.2s" in `text-waiting` or "arrived in 840 ms" muted (`durationText`; `tint` on the selected row). A selected waiting boundary's answer (`suspenseAnswer(cause, ms)`, `src/answer.ts`, ticking with the clock): "Showing its fallback for 1.2s, " then "waiting on Reviews (server)", "waiting on 1 promise thrown by Comments" ("2 promises"), "waiting inside Comments", "loading a lazy() component" or "waiting on a promise"; until the inspection says, only "Showing its fallback for 1.2s." (no guess). An arrived one with `suspense.awaited` has a "Waited on" section: "getReviews · Reviews · 1.2s".
- Server Components (M7 #79): for a `server` node the answer reads "Ran on the server."; Props are read-only (no `editable-value`, no editor); there's no hint, Renders section or Force re-render; the source row reads "Rendered at page.jsx:50". An Awaited section lists `server.awaits` (`[data-testid=server-row]` "getProduct 302 ms", `durationText`: whole ms, seconds with one decimal from 1,000 ms) and a Client components section `server.rendered` (a `NodeButton`, shared with Rendered by: hover highlights, click reveals; then `sizeText`). A component with `fromServer` shows, above the render answer, `[data-testid=server-answer]` "Server Component ProductDetails passed it 2 props, 14.3 KB" (`fromServerOf` in `src/answer.ts`; the name a node link when the page knows its id) and one `[data-testid=size-hint]` per prop with `fields`: "product is 14.3 KB, mostly specs (13.9 KB), name (12 B) and id (6 B). Pass AddToCart only the fields it uses."; a "Props from ProductDetails" section lists each prop and its size. `sizeText` (`src/size.ts`): under 1,000 bytes "N B", else KB with one decimal, past the page's caps "over N KB".
- Sources (`src/source.ts`, `createSourceResolver(fetch)`): a `{ file }` source (React 18) is itself. A `{ url }` frame (React 19) is read only from an `http(s)` script: its last `//# sourceMappingURL=`, inline (`data:`, base64 or percent-encoded) or an `http(s)` `.map` (sectioned maps too, Next's), resolved with `@jridgewell/trace-mapping` `AnyMap` (no dynamic code: docs/check.md; 1-based columns in and out). A source URL becomes a path: `file:` its path (Next: absolute), `http(s)` its pathname without the leading slash (Vite: `src/Counter.jsx`, relative to the dev server's root). No map or no mapping: the frame's own script path. Scripts and maps are fetched once per script URL for the panel's lifetime (a failed load is retried); anything else resolves to no location. A `file:` URL (M7 #79: a Server Component's server chunk) needs `origin` (`createSourceResolver(fetch, origin)`, `main.tsx` passes `editor.origin`): its map is fetched from `<origin>/__nextjs_source-map?filename=<encoded url>`, Next's dev server's endpoint for server chunks' maps; no origin, no map or no mapping resolves to nothing (the chunk's own path is no use to open). Requests use the extension's host permission; the page can only point them at URLs it could load itself, and the results are shown as text.
- Open in editor (`src/editor.ts`, `openInEditor(location, io)`): to the inspected page's origin (`inspectedWindow.eval("location.origin")`; Firefox resolves `[result, exception]`, Chrome before 151 only calls back). No server detection: Vite's `GET /__open-in-editor?file=<file>:<line>:<column>` (launch-editor-middleware: always 200 and empty; relative paths resolve against the server's cwd; editor from `LAUNCH_EDITOR`), then Next's `GET /__nextjs_launch-editor?file=<file>&line1=<n>&column1=<n>` (204 opened, 404 no such file; editor from `REACT_EDITOR`). Only an empty 2xx counts, so an app's catch-all page doesn't. Else `file:line:column` is copied with a selected textarea and `execCommand("copy")` (the Clipboard API needs a focused document, which a DevTools panel often isn't).
- Rendered by: the owners nearest first (`[data-testid=owner]`). One in the tree is an accent text button that calls `tree.reveal(id)` (and clears the hover first: selecting replaces the list, so no pointer-leave follows); hovering it calls `tree.hover(id)` and leaving `tree.hover(undefined)`, so the page overlay draws it just as for its tree row (select, expand its ancestors; `main.tsx` then inspects it); one that isn't (a Server Component) is muted text.
- `previewText(value)` (`src/value.ts`): DevTools-console-like one-liners: `"text"` (over 50 chars cut, with the full length), `ƒ name()`, `Symbol(x)`, `{a: 1, b: "x"}` and `[1, 2]` inline up to 5 entries (nested containers as `{...}`, `Array(n)`, `Map(n)`), `Array(n)` past 5 items, a class name before an instance's braces, `<Counter key="k" />`, `<button#id.class>`, `(getter)`, `empty`, `[circular]`, `(unreadable: message)`.
- `test/Inspector.test.tsx`, `test/value.test.ts`.

## Updates (`createTimelineStore`, `src/timeline.ts`; `Commits`, `src/Commits.tsx`; M6 #67, #69, #74)

- Tabs (`Tabs` in `src/ConnectionList.tsx`): with a `timeline` (`main.tsx` passes one; tests without it get the plain split), a `role="tablist"` "Views" above everything: "Components" (Toolbar, trees, Inspector) and "Updates" (#74; named by `aria-label`, its update count after the name: `count` is a function, since a reactive tab list rebuilt and remounted both panels on every update). `Tabs` reads `props.tabs` once (`list`, a memo): each read of the prop builds every tab's content again, and reading it in the tab ids mounted a throwaway `TreeView` (a whole-tree walk) about ten times per update. Each tab is a `role="tab"` button (`aria-selected`, `aria-controls`, roving `tabIndex`; Left/Right move and focus). Both `role="tabpanel"`s stay mounted, the inactive one `hidden` (Tailwind's preflight makes `[hidden]` `display: none !important`, over `flex`), so a switch keeps scroll, selection and focus state. The tab is a signal in `ConnectionList` (`COMPONENTS`/`UPDATES`) so links can switch it. Replaced the bar strip above the trees (#67), whose 7 px bars were hard to read and click and, 100 of them, overflowed a narrow panel and hid the newest.
- Store: the page's commit summaries (`commits`, `docs/messages.md`) appended; each message drops the commits below its `oldest` (the page bounds the list, #71), unpicking (`live()`) when the pick was among them, and sets `dropped()`. `shown(history)`: newest first; while `filtered()` (`setFiltered`), only the commits in `history` (the selected node's, `inspector.history()`). `picked()` the picked seq (none: nothing picked, the inspector shows the latest). `detail()` the picked commit's renders and triggers: `undefined` while loading, `null` once released, else `{ renders, updaters }`, `renders` appended across its `committed` batches, `updaters` from the first (a batch for another seq is ignored). `pick(seq)` sends `{ type: "commit", seq }`, clears the detail and pins the inspector (`inspector.pin`); `live()` unpicks and unpins. `key(key, history)` steps through `shown(history)`: ArrowDown older (from none, the newest), ArrowUp newer, Home newest, End oldest, Escape `live()`; true if handled. `reset()` on a tree `reset` (a new watch of the same document, e.g. after the background stopped): empties the list and `dropped()`, keeping the pick (and the inspector's pin and the detail) unless the re-sent buffer's `oldest` is past it. `clear()` on a navigation (`main.tsx`'s `onNavigated`): empties the list and `dropped()` and unpicks, as a new document's seqs start over. `setWasted(on)` (#74) keeps only updates with `wasted > 0`, with Only as well. `clearUpdates()` sends `{ type: "clear-updates" }` (the page empties its buffered updates, keeping counts and latest reasons), empties the list and unpicks. `rows(history)` (#74) turns `shown` into `UpdateRow`s: an update, or a group of 2+ consecutive updates with the same cause (`updaters` and `change.hook`), `id` its oldest member's seq, `wasted` summed, open while it holds the pick unless `setGroup(id, open)` says otherwise (a pick resets those), its members following as `member` updates. `key`: Left and Right close and open the pick's group; Up and Down step through every update in `shown` order (entering a group opens it).
- Inspector store `pin(seq)`: every node follows the pinned commit, a node selected later too (applied on its first inspection): if its `history` holds the seq it loads that render (`reason`; the newest is just followed), else `absent()` is true. `pin(undefined)` returns to the newest render.
- Arrivals and waterfalls (M7 #81): an update with `arrived` and no updaters reads "Data arrived · Reviews boundary · waited 840 ms" (" +1" per further arrival) instead of "Root render". `waterfalls(commits)` (`src/waterfall.ts`) chains the arrivals' awaits sorted by start: an await joins a chain when it starts 0 to 5 ms (`GAP_MS`) after the chain's last await ends; chains of 2+ are a `Waterfall` `{ id, seqs, waits, ms }` (`id` the newest member seq, `ms` first start to last end), across commits that needn't be adjacent (on `/shop` CartCount arrives between Reviews and Recommendations), or within one. `rows()` puts a `{ kind: "waterfall" }` row at its newest member's place, its members out of the main list and following it while open (`setGroup`, as for groups; a pick of a member opens it; Left and Right close and open the pick's waterfall). It reads "Waterfall · 2 waits, one after another · 2.0s", then the newest member's time; open, `[data-testid=waterfall]` inside the row's option lists each wait ("getReviews · Reviews · 1.2s", `[data-testid=waterfall-label]`) with a `bg-waiting` bar on a shared axis (`left`/`width` as % of `ms`), then `[data-testid=waterfall-hint]`: "getRecommendations in Recommendations started only after getReviews ended. Starting it alongside would save up to 802 ms." (the second wait). The list keeps focus itself (`aria-activedescendant`), so the keyboard reaches a waterfall by picking one of its updates.
- List (`Commits`, #74): a toolbar of `aria-pressed` toggles "All" (clears both filters), "With wasted renders", "Only <selected name>" (disabled with nothing selected), then "Clear". A `role="listbox"` "Updates" (`tabIndex 0`, the one tab stop, `aria-activedescendant` the picked row) of `role="option"` rows, two `[data-testid=line]` lines each: an update `update-<seq>` (`data-seq`) reads its cause, the first updater's name and `change` ("Counter: 2 → 3", previews; unlabeled: the page sends the hook's index only) and "+N" more updaters, or "Root render", then "3 renders · 2 wasted · 2s ago" (wasted left out at 0); a group `group-<id>` (`data-group`, `data-open` and a triangle: an option has no `aria-expanded`) reads "Shown · 3 updates" then "6 wasted · 2s ago", a click toggling it; its members are indented and lead with their change ("6 → 7"). No row says "commit" or shows a seq. Clicks and keys are handled once on the list (`timeline.key`; Escape stops propagation, DevTools opens its drawer on it). Empty: an `Empty` screen (#95, a list glyph) "No updates yet." and "Use the app: each commit React makes shows here." Once `dropped()`, "Older updates dropped (limit reached)" under the list.
- Detail (`[data-testid=commit-detail]`, `aria-label` "Update", beside the list, below it under 640 px): nothing picked: "Pick an update to see what rendered and why."; loading: nothing; released: "This update is no longer recorded."; otherwise the cause, one `[data-testid=commit-trigger]` line per updater (`NodeLink`, then " set State #1: 3 → 4, …" or " updated"), "Root render" for none; `[data-testid=commit-cost]` "4 components rendered · 1 had a reason, 3 only because a parent rendered"; then "What rendered" with a "Hide renders with no reason" checkbox (on): `cascade(renders, tree)` nests each render under its nearest ancestor that also rendered (`tree.parentOf` chain), `[data-testid=commit-render]` lines with `data-depth`, name and `KIND_TEXT` kinds; 2+ consecutive same-named siblings with the same kinds fold into "Row ×3 Props changed" (kinds, not values: those take a request per component). While hiding, wasted renders (kinds exactly `parent`) leave the cascade (their children attach to the nearest shown ancestor) and one `[data-testid=commit-hidden]` line reads "38 wasted, hidden".
- Links: a name in the detail (`onReveal`) switches to Components and `tree.reveal(id)`s it, the inspector still pinned to the commit; the Inspector's `onRenders` filters and switches to Updates, `onCommit(seq)` picks and switches, `onLatest` calls `timeline.live()`.
- Wiring: `main.tsx` creates the store (commands to the port with the tab, like the inspector's) and feeds it `commits` and `committed` (the relay forwards both after `parseCommits`/`parseCommitted`); a tree batch starting with `reset` resets it.
- `test/timeline.test.ts`, `test/Commits.test.tsx`, `test/ConnectionList.test.tsx` (tabs, links), `test/inspection.test.ts`.

## Tree view (`TreeView`, `src/TreeView.tsx`, `src/virtual.ts`; M3 #26)

One per development root: `TreeView(props: { tree: TreeStore; rootId: number })`.

- Virtual list: `[data-testid=tree]` (`role="tree"`, focusable, not a scroller) holds a spacer of `rows × ROW_HEIGHT` (20px) and only the window of rows `windowOf(top, height, count)` returns: the rows in the pane's view plus `OVERSCAN` (10) each side. `top` is the pane's view top in the tree's coordinates (the tree's offset from the pane's top, negated: negative while the tree starts below the view, and an empty window once it's entirely below), `height` the pane's `clientHeight`. The pane is the closest `[data-testid=trees]`, else `document.documentElement` (unit tests). Measured on mount, on the pane's `scroll`, and from a `ResizeObserver` on the pane (the panel's size) and on the tree (trees above it change its offset). jsdom has no `ResizeObserver`: `test/setup.ts` stubs one for the `panel` Vitest project. Fixed row height keeps the window arithmetic and unit-testable without layout (`test/virtual.test.ts`).
- Rows (`[data-testid=node]`, `role="treeitem"`, `aria-level`, `aria-selected`, `aria-expanded` when expandable, `data-id`): a toggle (`[data-toggle]` area, `[data-testid=toggle]` CSS-border triangle, rotated when expanded; no text so the e2e text readers don't take it for a name), the name, a `[data-testid=badge]` for `memo`/`forwardRef`/`lazy`, and `[data-testid=key]` as one text node `key="…"`. All page data is text nodes.
- Selected row: `bg-selected`, badge and key `text-fg` (dark `muted` on `selected` is 2.9:1). The rows' wrapper is `w-max min-w-full` (as wide as the widest row in the window, at least the pane's content), so in a tree deeper than the pane every row, and the selection's background, spans the sideways scroll.
- Search matches: `data-match`, and the name (`[data-testid=name]`) in `text-accent`, except on the selected row (`text-fg`; accent on `selected` isn't a checked contrast pair).
- Clicks and keys are handled once on the container: rows are recycled as the window moves, and the container holds focus. A click on an expandable row's toggle area toggles it; any other row click selects. Handled keys (`tree.key`) are `preventDefault`ed.
- Hover: a delegated `onPointerOver` hovers the row under the pointer; `onPointerLeave` on the tree clears it. Pointer rather than mouse events because Biome's a11y rule asks for a focus counterpart to `onMouseOver`; keyboard selection doesn't highlight the page (not in M3's scope).
- A selection change scrolls the pane to the selected row, keeping a row's height clear of the top and bottom edges (macOS draws the horizontal scrollbar over the content; less in a pane under three rows tall) (End on 10,000 rows renders the last one), then sideways: it renders the new window at once (`measure()`; the scroll event comes later) and, on the next animation frame (the scroll applied, the window rendered), scrolls so the row's content (its toggle to its last child: name, badge or key, plus a row's height of room at the right, where macOS draws the vertical scrollbar over the content) is whole in view when it fits; content wider than the pane is scrolled to its start (the toggle at the left edge). Whole pixels, rounded outward. It also runs on every `reveal` (picker, search, owners), counted by `tree.reveals()`, so picking the selected component again scrolls back to it. `reveal` selects and expands ancestors in one `batch`, so this sees the revealed row: selecting first left it scrolling to a row that wasn't there yet.
- A selection made while the pane is 0 px tall (DevTools showing another panel, as Elements after Show in Elements panel, #92) can't scroll then: it waits by animation frames for the pane to have a height and scrolls to the selection once. Not a `ResizeObserver`: Chrome sends a hidden panel no resize, so coming back matches the last size it reported.
- Render counts (M6 #72): `tree.receiveCounts(counts)` (the page's `counts`, `docs/messages.md`) keeps `{ renders, wasted }` per id, emptied with the tree (a `reset` op, `clear()`; a watch sends them all again). A row with `renders > 1` ends with a muted `[data-testid=renders]` number, `ml-auto` at the tree's right edge (a mount alone says nothing); the reveal scroll's sideways step ignores it. The ids in the newest counts message (the page's last 100 ms flush) are recent (`tree.isRecent(id)`) for `RECENT_MS` (1 s; a newer message replaces the set and restarts it): `data-recent` and `bg-highlight/40`, under the selection's `bg-selected`. Counts and recency aren't in `Row`: each row reads `countOf`/`isRecent`, which track their own signal, so a counts message (every flush) and its fade update the shown rows in place. In `rows()` they rebuilt every row object, so `For` replaced every row element on each flush. Under the trees pane (`ConnectionList`) a muted legend: "Numbers: renders since DevTools opened".
- Groups (M6 #72): in `tree.rows()`, a run of `GROUP_MIN` (5) or more consecutive visible siblings with the same name and kind (keys may differ) is one row: id minus the first member's (a negative id is never a node), the shared name and kind, no key, `group: { size }`; `countOf(groupId)` is the members' wasted summed and `isRecent(groupId)` any member's; `[data-testid=group]` "×40 · 195 wasted" (no wasted part at 0), collapsed by default. Open while any member is in `opened`: `toggle(groupId)` adds the first member or removes them all (the members as the last `rows()` found them); `reveal(id)` (pick, search, owners, links) adds the id and its ancestors, so a revealed member's group opens. Members follow their group a level deeper. Keys: Left goes to the nearest earlier row a level up (a member's group), Right opens a closed group. A selected group stays selected across batches while its first member exists (`Math.abs`), but isn't a component: `main.tsx` inspects only ids above 0 (the Inspector clears) and hovering it highlights nothing.
- Server Components (M7 #78): a `server` node (`docs/page.md`, Tree) is a row like any other (select, keys, search, hover) with a `server` badge in `text-server`. `Row.client` marks where client code starts: a component kind (`COMPONENT_KINDS`: function, class, forwardRef, memo, lazy, server) other than `server` whose nearest component ancestor (Suspense, providers and DOM elements skipped; `Node.scope`, set on add) is a server node; the row adds `[data-testid=client]` "client" in `text-client`. Next's client components arrive as lazy client references, so they read "AddToCart lazy client". Badge and mark are `text-fg` when selected (`tint(id, token)`).
- Next.js internals (M7 #78, `src/next.ts`): `nextInternal(name, kind, parent)` is true for `"<kind> <name>"` entries from Next 16.4.6's App Router tree (`NEXT_INTERNALS`; by kind, so Next's function `ErrorBoundary` is one and an app's class `ErrorBoundary` isn't), any name starting `__next_`, an unnamed `Context` provider under an internal, and a `Suspense` under a `__next_` node. `parent` is the nearest non-DOM node above (Next wraps its metadata Suspense in a `div`). `Node.internal` is set on add and on rename. They're hidden (`visible()`; children take their place, no search match, a hidden selection clears) only in a root holding a function `AppRouter` (`nextRoots`), so a Vite app's own `Router` or `Head` stays; `showInternals()` / `setShowInternals(on)` (off by default) brings them back. `hiddenCount()` counts Next roots' internals (kept per root on add and `forget`). The legend bar under the trees (`ConnectionList`) adds, while it's above 0, ` · <span data-testid=hidden-count>52 Next.js components hidden</span>` (or "shown") and an accent text button `Show` (or `Hide`). On `/shop`, 77 are hidden and the tree starts at `RootLayout`.
- Perf marks: `main.tsx` marks `reactdx:subscribe` on every subscribe; `TreeView` marks `reactdx:rows` each time its rows go from empty to non-empty. `e2e/perf.test.ts` reads them (`docs/e2e.md`).
- `test/TreeView.test.tsx`: a 1,000-row tree keeps fewer than 100 rows in the DOM, badges, keys and toggles, text-only keys, click, toggle and keyboard, match marking, render counts and the recent mark, group rows, the server badge and client mark. `test/tree.test.ts`: counts, recent, grouping and group keys, client marks, hidden Next internals. `test/next.test.ts`: the internals rules.

## Toolbar (`Toolbar`, `src/Toolbar.tsx`; M3 #27)

Above the copies, only when a development copy is present (`ConnectionList`), so the no-React and production notices stay exactly as they were.

Laid out like SnapQL's search bar (`~/Code/snapql/apps/extension/src/panel/search.tsx`): a `<search>` bar `h-10`, its buttons copied from SnapQL's `IconButton`.

- `Pick element` icon button (`[data-testid=pick]`, crosshair icon; the name is its `aria-label` and `title`; `aria-pressed` from `picking()`, `bg-accent/20 text-accent` when on).

- Search field: a rounded `bg-surface` label filling the bar (search icon, accent focus ring) around the input (`[data-testid=search]`, `aria-label="Search components"`, bound to `query()`, native cancel button hidden): input sets the query; Enter steps to the next match, Shift+Enter to the previous.
- Keys (#95): `/` anywhere in the panel focuses the search (a document `keydown` listener, default prevented), unless a modifier is held, the target is an input, textarea or contenteditable (the Inspector's search, a value editor), or the Components tab is hidden (Updates in front). Esc in the search clears it.
- No matches (#95): search marks matches without filtering rows, so while the query matches nothing a `[data-testid=no-match]` row tops the trees pane (`ConnectionList.tsx`, sticky at the left): `No components match “<query>”.` and a "Clear search" button (`setQuery("")`).
- Inside the field, only while there's a query: the counter (`[data-testid=search-count]`, `<position> of <matches>`: "1 of 3" after typing, "0 of 0" with no matches) and a `Clear search` icon button.
- `Show DOM elements` icon button (`[data-testid=show-dom]`, `</>` icon, the name as `aria-label` and `title`, `aria-pressed`, accent when on): `setShowHosts`. An icon rather than a labelled pill, so the search field keeps the bar's width.
- Outline modes, one at a time (`tree.outlines()`: an `OutlineMode` or undefined, off by default): `Outline Suspense on the page` (M7 #82, `[data-testid=outlines]`, dashed rectangle), `Light client islands` (M7 #83, `[data-testid=islands]`, half-filled square) and `Flash renders on the page` (#91, `[data-testid=flash]`, a box with rays); pressing one sets its mode (replacing the other), pressing it again turns outlines off. Without a server node in the tree (`tree.hasServers()`, a count kept on add and remove) the islands button is disabled with the title "No Server Components on this page": `IconButton`'s `reason` disables it and becomes its title (the `aria-label` stays its name, so the reason is its accessible description). `main.tsx` posts `OutlinesMessage { mode }` on each change (`null` for off), and the mode again on a batch starting with `reset` while one is set: a new document's agent (a reload) starts with outlines off. Closing the panel unwatches, which turns them off on the page.
- `test/Toolbar.test.tsx`: counter, Enter and Shift+Enter, no matches, clearing, the DOM toggle, the picker button, the outlines toggles.

## Elements panel (`src/elements.ts`; #92)

- `followElements({ onSelectionChanged, evaluate })` `{ show(id) }`: each selection change in the browser's Elements panel evaluates `SELECT_CODE`, which dispatches `ELEMENTS_EVENT` with `{ selected: $0 }`; `show(id)` evaluates `showCode(id)`, an IIFE that dispatches `{ id }`, calls `inspect(detail.element)` when the agent filled it, and returns whether it did. The agent's side: `docs/page.md`, Elements panel.
- `main.tsx` passes `browser.devtools.panels.elements.onSelectionChanged` and `evaluate(code)`, the one page eval (also `location.origin` for the editor): Firefox resolves `[result, exception]`, Chrome before 151 only calls back. The panel page exists once ReactDX's tab was first shown, so selections before that aren't followed.
- `test/elements.test.ts`: the wiring with a fake API; both code strings run with `new Function("$0", "inspect", ...)` against a jsdom listener.

## Themes (`src/themes.ts`, `src/index.css`)

Copied from SnapQL (`~/Code/snapql/apps/extension/src/panel/themes.ts`, `index.css`), so both extensions look the same.

- Themes are data: `Theme = { id, name, kind, colors: Record<ColorToken, string> }`, tokens `bg, fg, muted, border, selected, error, surface, accent, success, syntax-key, syntax-string, syntax-number, highlight`. `highlight` is search matches' background (DevTools' search yellows, light `#fde293`, dark `#594500`); `fg` on it is checked at 4.5:1. Ships `devtools-light`, `devtools-dark` with SnapQL's values.
  - `bg`, `fg`, `selected`, `error` and dark `muted` come from the DevTools document's `--sys-color-*` variables (source noted in the file).
  - SnapQL's own: `border`, light `muted` `#5f6368` (DevTools' `#757575` is 4.14:1 on `surface`), `surface`, `accent`, `success`, `syntax-*`.
  - M7 #78 adds `server` (`#8430ce` / `#d7aefb`), `client` (`#a04f00` / `#f9ab68`) and `waiting` (`#8a5a00` / `#fdd663`) for server rows, client marks and Suspense waits (light / dark), each at least 4.5:1 on `bg` and `surface`.
  - `test/themes.test.ts` pins every value and checks every text token (`fg`, `muted`, `error`, `success`, `accent`, `syntax-*`) is at least 4.5:1 on `bg` and `surface`. Dark `muted` on `selected` is 2.9:1, so selected rows must not rely on `muted`.
- `defaultTheme(kind)` picks by DevTools kind. Adding a theme is one entry in `themes`.
- `applyTheme(theme, root)`: sets `--theme-<token>` (`themeVars`), `data-theme=<id>`, `data-theme-kind=<kind>` and `color-scheme: <kind>` (native scrollbars and form controls otherwise stay light).
- `index.css`:
  - `@import "tailwindcss" source(".")`: Tailwind scans `packages/panel/src` (the CSS is built from `apps/extension`, outside it).
  - `@theme { --color-*: initial; }` drops Tailwind's default palette, so `bg-red-500` generates nothing. Components use token classes only (`bg-bg`, `text-muted`, `border-border`), never a theme name or color. `apps/extension/test/build.test.ts` plants a palette class to prove it.
  - `@theme inline` maps `--color-<token>` to `--theme-<token>`.
  - Biome needs `css.parser.tailwindDirectives` (`biome.json`).
- Type: labels `font-sans` 12px (`text-xs`), page data `font-mono` (M2 list onwards).
- Exports: `@reactdx/panel` (`Panel`), `@reactdx/panel/tree`, `@reactdx/panel/themes`, `@reactdx/panel/index.css`.

## Theme source (`apps/extension/entrypoints/panel/theme.ts`, `main.tsx`)

- `getTheme()`: `browser.devtools.panels.themeName === "dark"` at load. `onThemeChanged` in Firefox only.
- Chrome has no theme event, and its panel iframe's `prefers-color-scheme` flips during load (seen in SnapQL's e2e), so Chrome keeps the load-time theme until the panel reopens.
- The panel needs `browser.devtools`, so it only runs inside DevTools; `panel.html` opened as a tab throws.
- e2e: `e2e/theme.test.ts` (Chrome) launches DevTools light and dark and checks the panel's `data-theme`, `color-scheme` and `--theme-bg` (`docs/e2e.md`).
